cards.title: Which size was off?
cards.text: You marked the maze sizes as a problem with no comment. Which one?
cards.why: I can't tell which number bothered you. Each is now a setting, so whichever it was can be tried both ways.

options.label: The whole maze
options.text: 24×24 squares: a long way to walk.

options.label: Camera distance
options.text: How much of the maze fits on screen.

cards.details: My guess is the whole maze: 24×24 squares is about 240 cells across, and with endless runs you'd rarely see most of it. Settings now have Small (16), Medium (24) and Large (32).

cards.title: Corridor sets
cards.text: The four corridor sets, from above with see-all on. Tick the ones to keep.
cards.why: Width decides whether a horde is a wall or something you run round.

items.label: Mixed
items.text: Mostly 3 wide, 4-wide roads to the corners, 2-wide tunnels into dead ends. Your pick last time.

items.label: All 3 wide
items.text: Every corridor three of you wide.

items.label: All 2 wide
items.text: Tight. A crowd fills a corridor.

cards.title: Camera distance
cards.text: How far out the camera sits. Tick the ones to keep.
cards.why: Closer looks bigger and reads better on a phone; farther shows what's coming.

cards.title: How rounds come back
cards.text: How should a weapon get its rounds back?
cards.why: You wanted rounds that differ per weapon. Trickle-back means you never quite run dry; a full reload means a gap to plan for.

options.label: One by one
options.text: Rounds trickle back after a short pause (all three now).

options.label: Full reload
options.text: Empty the magazine, then a reload refills it all.

options.label: Each weapon picks
options.text: Pistol trickles, SMG reloads all at once, and so on.

cards.title: Where firing lives
cards.text: Is how a weapon fires (let go, hold, auto) part of the weapon, so modules can change it?
cards.why: If it's part of the weapon, a pistol and an SMG are different weapons with the same Bolt shape. If it's a module, any cast could be made hold-to-fire, which is more freedom but one more slot spent.
cards.pick: Part of the weapon. Some modules change it: Charge turns let-go into hold-to-charge.
cards.details: Same goes for the summon (cooldown) and the dash (charges): each cast has a trigger and its own way of getting uses back, and modules can bend both. This decides how the next stage's Spawn and Dash casts are built.

cards.title: Crowds hold you
cards.text: Enemies push back on you, so a packed corridor holds you until you dash or shoot through?
cards.why: Without it you walk through any crowd and the maze isn't dangerous. With it, dead ends are real traps.
